summary: This informational RFC updates RFC 7315 by changing the extension-access-info part of the SIP P-Access-Network-Info header ABNF, and adding two access-info parameter values, operator-specific-GI and utran-sai-3gpp, that were defined but missing from the list.

eli5.summary: A grammar fix: two allowed values were described but not listed, so this adds them.

questions: what does rfc 7913 change in rfc 7315
subtitle: A grammar fix for the SIP P-Access-Network-Info header that adds two missing values and loosens the extension rule.

tldr.problem: The ABNF for the P-Access-Network-Info header in RFC 7315 forced new access-info values to follow the stricter gen-value rule, and left two defined values out of the list.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7913 changes extension-access-info from gen-value to generic-param and adds operator-specific-GI and utran-sai-3gpp to the access-info list.
tldr.outcome: The grammar now matches how values were already being defined, and the change is not considered to cause backward compatibility problems.

today: RFC 7913 is an Informational document that updates RFC 7315, and no later RFC is listed as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: The Problem in the Grammar
sections.content:
RFC 7315 defines the Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) P-Access-Network-Info header field. Its syntax has an access-info parameter with a set of pre-defined values. Most of them follow the generic-param rule from RFC 3261.

However, the ABNF in RFC 7315 required new values to follow the gen-value rule, which is more restrictive. The RFC says there is no justification for the restriction, and new values have already been defined following generic-param.

Separately, the ABNF defines operator-specific-GI and utran-sai-3gpp but does not include them in the list of access-info values.
sections.eli5: One rule said new answers had to be written in a very strict way, even though nobody needed that. Two valid answers were also forgotten on the list.

sections.title: The ABNF Change
sections.content: The update modifies Section 5.4 of RFC 7315. In the old syntax, extension-access-info = gen-value. In the new syntax, extension-access-info = generic-param, and the access-info list gains operator-specific-GI and utran-sai-3gpp just before extension-access-info.
sections.eli5: Swap one strict rule for a looser one, and add two missing choices to the menu.

sections.title: Compatibility and Security
sections.content:
The header field is mainly used in networks defined by the 3rd-Generation Partnership Project (3GPP), where new values following generic-param have already been defined. For that reason the update is not considered to cause backward compatibility issues.

The security considerations stay as defined in RFC 7315, and the ABNF update does not impact them.
sections.eli5: Since the people using this already follow the looser rule, nothing breaks, and nothing becomes less safe.

data.title: Updated access-info rules
data.code:
access-info            = cgi-3gpp / utran-cell-id-3gpp /
                         dsl-location / i-wlan-node-id /
                         ci-3gpp2 / eth-location /
                         ci-3gpp2-femto / fiber-location /
                         np / gstn-location /local-time-zone /
                         dvb-rcs2-node-id / operator-specific-GI /
                         utran-sai-3gpp / extension-access-info
np                     = "network-provided"
extension-access-info  = generic-param

references.text: Rosenberg, J., et al., "SIP: Session Initiation Protocol", RFC 3261, June 2002.
Crocker, D., Ed. and P. Overell, "Augmented BNF for Syntax Specifications: ABNF", STD 68, RFC 5234, January 2008.
Jesske, R., Drage, K., and C. Holmberg, "Private Header (P-Header) Extensions to the Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) for the 3GPP", RFC 7315, July 2014.
